steps.title: Goal and explanation
steps.body: MOCK ORIGINAL LESSON. A variable is a named place for a current value. Input supplies a value, processing changes or combines values, and output reports a result. Read instructions from top to bottom. An assignment replaces the old value; it does not keep every earlier value.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Start with count = 2. First run count = count + 3, so count becomes 5. Then run count = count * 2, so count becomes 10. Displaying count outputs 10. Reversing the two assignments would produce 7, so their order matters.

steps.title: Guided check
steps.body: Apply the explanation, then inspect the corrective feedback.

steps.title: Explain the rule
steps.body: Before continuing, separate the current value from the instruction. If count is 4, the instruction count = count + 2 replaces it with 6. Only the next instruction sees that updated 6. Writing the value after every line prevents using the original input twice.

steps.title: Trace the order
steps.body: Arrange the steps using the labeled movement controls.

steps.title: Independent application
steps.body: Use the rule in this new small example.

steps.title: Summary and later review
steps.body: To trace a sequence independently, record each new value in order, then report the last value at the output instruction. Practice results here are demonstration study data, not a course grade.

questions.prompt: Which instruction is processing rather than input or output?

options.feedback: This combines two values to compute a new value.
Reading supplies input; it does not perform the multiplication.
Displaying reports the result after processing.

questions.hint: Look for the instruction that calculates a new value.
questions.explanation: Multiplication transforms the supplied values. Reading and displaying belong to the input and output stages.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to read a count, add three, then report it.

options.feedback: The value must be available before the assignment uses it.
Update the input before displaying the result.
Report the updated value after processing.

questions.hint: Supply a value, transform it, then report it.
questions.explanation: This ordering makes each instruction use a value that has already been supplied or computed.

questions.prompt: Start count = 4. Run count = count + 2, then count = count * 3. What value is displayed?
questions.hint: Write the value after the addition before applying the multiplication.
questions.explanation: The addition gives 6; the next line multiplies that 6 by 3 to give 18.

questions.prompt: In the input-process-output cycle, name the stage that calculates a changed value.
questions.explanation: Processing performs the calculation; input supplies values and output reports them.

questions.prompt: A new run starts count = 1, adds 4, then doubles the current count. What is its output?
questions.hint: Use the updated value 5 for the final step.
questions.explanation: One plus four gives five; doubling five gives ten.

glossary.definition: A value supplied to a program before a calculation uses it.
A name associated with a current value that assignments may replace.
An instruction that stores a calculated or supplied value in a variable.
A value or message that the program reports.
